metadata.title: zERC20 Privacy Token Protocol - Audit Map (Batch 5)

audit_results.title: Verify Verifier authenticates Hub before saving global root

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: Attacker sends crafted LayerZero message with spoofed source EID to inject unauthorized global root
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: _lzReceive validates origin.srcEid == $.hubEid at line 440 before any storage write. setPeer at LayerZero level provides additional sender validation. The check occurs before abi.decode of payload.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: Attacker deploys malicious contract and calls Verifier._lzReceive with srcEid=1 (unauthorized). Revert at line 440 with InvalidHubSource(1).

2_state_transition_violation.attack_description: Attacker attempts to overwrite existing globalTransferRoots entry with different value
2_state_transition_violation.analysis: Line 443 checks if ($.globalTransferRoots[aggSeq_] == 0) before writing. This ensures write-once semantics per aggSeq index. Duplicate messages are ignored silently.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: Hub broadcasts (root=A, aggSeq=5). Later, malicious replay attempts (root=B, aggSeq=5). Second write is skipped due to non-zero check at line 443.

3_resource_exhaustion.attack_description: Attacker spams valid global root saves to exhaust storage or gas
3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: Only Hub can send valid messages (srcEid check). Hub increments aggSeq atomically, preventing duplicate index attacks. Storage is O(n) where n = number of broadcasts, bounded by Hub's aggSeq counter.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: DoS via legitimate Hub broadcasts requires compromising Hub's aggSeq increment mechanism, which is atomic and owner-controlled.

4_faulty_error_handling.attack_description: Silent failures in _lzReceive could leave Verifier in inconsistent state
4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: _lzReceive uses require() for srcEid validation (line 440), which reverts on failure. Duplicate aggSeq handling is intentionally silent (skip, not revert) to avoid blocking LayerZero message delivery.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: If abi.decode fails for malformed payload, entire call reverts. No partial state update possible.

5_race_conditions.attack_description: Concurrent _lzReceive calls for same aggSeq could cause race condition
5_race_conditions.analysis: EVM transaction atomicity ensures only one transaction executes at a time. The check-then-write pattern at lines 443-444 is atomic within a single transaction.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: Two LayerZero messages with same aggSeq arrive. First sets globalTransferRoots[aggSeq]=root. Second sees non-zero value, skips write. No race condition.

audit_results.summary: Hub authentication via srcEid validation at line 440 is correctly implemented before any storage modification. Write-once semantics prevents root overwrite.

audit_results.title: Verify STATE-GLOBAL-ROOT-SAVED implies correct storage

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: Attacker provides invalid aggSeq index to corrupt storage
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: aggSeq_ is decoded from trusted Hub payload after srcEid validation. No additional validation needed as Hub controls aggSeq monotonicity.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: Malformed aggSeq would require Hub compromise. Hub only sends valid aggSeq values via broadcast().

2_state_transition_violation.attack_description: Event emission without storage write or vice versa
2_state_transition_violation.analysis: Storage write at line 444 occurs before event emission at line 445. Both are within the same if block, ensuring atomicity. Event only emitted on successful write.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: If storage write fails (out of gas), entire transaction reverts. Event cannot be emitted without storage update.

3_resource_exhaustion.attack_description: Storage expansion attack via large aggSeq values
3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: globalTransferRoots is a mapping(uint64 => uint256). Storage is allocated on-demand. Hub controls aggSeq progression, preventing sparse allocation attacks.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: Attacker cannot skip aggSeq values without Hub cooperation. Hub's aggSeq++ ensures sequential allocation.

4_faulty_error_handling.attack_description: Silent duplicate handling masks legitimate failures
4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: Duplicates are intentionally skipped without event. This is correct behavior for LayerZero message replay protection. No state corruption possible.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Duplicate message with same aggSeq: first saves root, second skips. Both valid behaviors.

5_race_conditions.attack_description: latestAggSeq update races with globalTransferRoots write
5_race_conditions.analysis: Both storage updates occur in same transaction. latestAggSeq is updated unconditionally if new aggSeq > current (line 448-450), independent of write-once check.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: aggSeq=10 arrives twice. First: saves root, updates latestAggSeq to 10. Second: skips root save, no-ops on latestAggSeq (10 not > 10).

audit_results.summary: State transition correctly stores root before emitting event. Write-once check ensures immutability per aggSeq index.

audit_results.title: Verify Indexer availability monitoring exists

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: N/A - Off-chain service state, no on-chain attack vector
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: Indexer is an off-chain service. Its availability is an operational concern, not a smart contract security property.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: Indexer downtime prevents proof generation but does not compromise on-chain security.

2_state_transition_violation.attack_description: N/A - No on-chain state machine for indexer
2_state_transition_violation.analysis: Indexer state is purely off-chain. On-chain contracts do not depend on indexer availability for security.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: Even with indexer offline, on-chain proofs remain valid and verifiable.

3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: Indexer resource exhaustion is operational, not security-critical.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: Indexer DoS delays proof generation but does not affect protocol security.

4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: Error handling in indexer is operational best practice, not security-critical.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Indexer crashes are recoverable without protocol impact.

5_race_conditions.analysis: Race conditions in indexer are operational concerns.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: Concurrent indexer operations do not affect on-chain state integrity.

audit_results.summary: Off-chain indexer service availability is operational responsibility. Security verification requires off-chain service audit.

audit_results.title: Verify Indexer captures all IndexedTransfer events without loss

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: N/A - Off-chain event subscription
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: Event capture is off-chain operation. Missing events cause proof generation failure, caught by on-chain verification.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: If indexer misses event, generated proof will fail on-chain verification (hash chain mismatch).

2_state_transition_violation.analysis: Indexer state tracking is independent of on-chain state machine.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: Incorrect indexer state cannot affect on-chain contract state.

3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: On-chain transfer events require valid ERC20 transfers with gas costs. Spam is economically constrained.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: Each transfer requires gas payment, limiting spam rate. Indexer can process events asynchronously.

4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: RPC retry logic is operational. Any missed events result in proof verification failure.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Indexer RPC failure -> retry -> eventual consistency. Proof fails if events missed.

5_race_conditions.analysis: Reorg handling is operational concern. Indexer should wait for finality before processing.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: Indexer processes reorged block, proof uses invalid hash chain, on-chain verification fails.

audit_results.summary: Event capture integrity is self-verifying: missing events cause on-chain proof rejection. Off-chain audit required for operational assurance.

audit_results.title: Verify Adaptor is stateless and ready for bridge requests

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: Attacker exploits stale state in Adaptor
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: Adaptor tracks per-user balances (zerc20Balances, nativeBalances, underlyingTokenBalances) for multi-step operations. Each operation debits balances atomically via _debit* functions.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: Stale balance attack: User A deposits 100 zERC20. Adaptor records balance. User A withdraws. Balance debited. No stale state exploitable.

2_state_transition_violation.attack_description: Adaptor left in blocking state preventing future calls
2_state_transition_violation.analysis: nonReentrant modifier prevents recursive calls but releases after function completion. No persistent blocking state. Try-catch in _unwrapAndBridge prevents revert propagation.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: Call fails mid-operation -> try-catch catches -> balances preserved -> next call succeeds.

3_resource_exhaustion.attack_description: Attacker fills balance mappings to increase storage costs
3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: Balance storage per user requires token deposit with economic cost. Spam users costs attacker gas and tokens.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: Creating 1M entries requires 1M token deposits + gas.

4_faulty_error_handling.attack_description: Silent failures leave Adaptor in inconsistent state
4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: Try-catch blocks emit events on failure (lines 403, 413, 424, 436). Balances preserved on failure. User can withdraw via withdraw() function.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Bridge fails -> BridgeUnderlyingTokenFailed event emitted -> user calls withdraw() -> funds recovered.

5_race_conditions.attack_description: Concurrent lzCompose and withdraw calls race on balance
5_race_conditions.analysis: Both functions have nonReentrant modifier. EVM transaction atomicity ensures balance updates are sequential.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: lzCompose and withdraw in separate txs. Each tx is atomic. No race condition possible.

audit_results.summary: Adaptor maintains per-user balances for multi-step operations. nonReentrant and try-catch ensure no blocking state. Recovery via withdraw() function.

audit_results.title: Verify bridge request validation including slippage limits

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: Attacker bypasses minAmountOut validation for slippage attack
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: _validateBridgeRequest validates to != address(0) and dstEid != 0 (lines 385-386). minAmountOut check at line 409: if (amountOutput < request.minAmountOut) triggers zERC20 bridge back. _bridgeUnderlyingToken rechecks at line 480-481.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: User sets minAmountOut=100. Quote shows output=90. Line 409 check fails -> zERC20 sent back instead of low-output bridge.

2_state_transition_violation.analysis: Slippage violation triggers bridgeZerc20Self to return tokens to user. No bridge initiated when minAmountOut not met.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: minAmountOut exceeded -> zERC20 bridged back -> user receives original tokens.

3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: quoteFee is view function wrapped in try-catch. Failed quote emits QuoteFailed event and returns early. No storage writes on quote failure.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: Malicious quote -> catches failure -> returns without state change.

4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: decodeBridgeRequest wrapped in try-catch. Decode failure emits DecodeBridgeRequestFailed event and returns early. No funds at risk.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Malformed message -> decode fails -> event emitted -> tokens credited to user balance for withdrawal.

5_race_conditions.attack_description: Quote changes between quote and execution
5_race_conditions.analysis: Quote is calculated in same transaction. TOCTOU attack requires manipulating LiquidityManager state between quoteFee and unwrapSelf in same tx - impossible with nonReentrant.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: Quote + unwrap in same atomic tx. No external state change possible between them.

audit_results.summary: Bridge validation correctly enforces slippage limits with fallback to zERC20 return. Try-catch ensures graceful failure handling.

audit_results.title: Verify Adaptor correctly invokes LiquidityManager for unwrap

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: Adaptor bypasses LiquidityManager for direct token transfer
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: _unwrap function calls LIQUIDITY_MANAGER.unwrap(amount, address(this)) at line 457. No direct token transfer path exists. All unwrap operations go through LiquidityManager.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: Search Adaptor.sol for transfer/safeTransfer of underlying: only found in withdraw() which debits from underlyingTokenBalances, not mints new tokens.

2_state_transition_violation.analysis: Balance tracking: underlyingTokenBalanceBefore (line 454), unwrap call (line 457), underlyingTokenBalanceAfter (line 460), actualAmountOut calculation (line 461). Multiple checks ensure consistency.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: LM returns 100, but balance only increases by 90 -> line 465 reverts with AmountMismatch.

3_resource_exhaustion.attack_description: Repeated unwrap calls exhausting LiquidityManager liquidity
3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: Unwrap requires burning zERC20. Each unwrap costs attacker zERC20 tokens. Economic constraint prevents spam.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: Unwrap spam requires equivalent zERC20 burn per call.

4_faulty_error_handling.attack_description: LiquidityManager unwrap failure leaves Adaptor in bad state
4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: unwrapSelf wrapped in try-catch. Failure emits UnwrapFailed event and returns early. User zERC20 balance preserved for later withdrawal.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: LM.unwrap reverts -> caught at line 422 -> event emitted -> user withdraws zERC20 via withdraw().

5_race_conditions.attack_description: Balance tracking race between debit and unwrap
5_race_conditions.analysis: _debitZerc20Balance called first (line 452), then unwrap (line 457). Atomic within transaction. nonReentrant prevents recursive calls.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: Debit + unwrap in same tx. No external call between them that could exploit race.

audit_results.summary: All unwrap paths correctly delegate to LiquidityManager. Balance tracking and consistency checks prevent fund discrepancies.

audit_results.title: Verify Stargate bridge enforces minAmountOut slippage protection

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: minAmountOut set to 0 allowing unlimited slippage
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: Line 480 checks: if (amountToBridge == 0 || amountToBridge < request.minAmountOut) revert OutputTooLow. User-specified minAmountOut passed to SendParam. Stargate enforces this limit.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: User sets minAmountOut=100. Bridge would return 90. Stargate reverts due to slippage limit.

2_state_transition_violation.analysis: Pre-check at line 409 and enforcement in _bridgeUnderlyingToken at line 480. Both must pass for bridge to proceed.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: Either check failing prevents bridge initiation.

3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: Fees quoted via Stargate.quoteSend in same transaction. Excess native fee refunded to user at line 489. No manipulation possible within atomic tx.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: Fee increases between quote and bridge in separate txs -> user sets appropriate buffer.

4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: bridgeUnderlyingTokenSelf wrapped in try-catch. Failure emits BridgeUnderlyingTokenFailed event. User's underlyingTokenBalances preserved for withdrawal.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Stargate reverts -> caught -> event emitted -> user calls withdraw(underlyingToken, amount).

5_race_conditions.analysis: Quote and execution in same transaction. No external state can change between them. minAmountOut is user-controlled slippage tolerance.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: All operations atomic. Price changes between blocks protected by user's minAmountOut setting.

audit_results.summary: minAmountOut correctly passed to Stargate and enforced at multiple levels. Failed bridges preserve user funds via balance tracking.

audit_results.title: Verify STATE-BRIDGE-INITIATED implies prior unwrap completion

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: Bridge initiated without prior unwrap
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: _unwrapAndBridge function: line 420 calls unwrapSelf first, line 430 calls bridgeUnderlyingTokenSelf only after successful unwrap. Sequential execution enforced.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: Unwrap fails at line 422 -> returns early -> bridge never called.

2_state_transition_violation.attack_description: Bridge state reached without unwrap state
2_state_transition_violation.analysis: unwrapSelf must return successfully (line 421) before bridgeUnderlyingTokenSelf called (line 430). Sequential try-catch blocks enforce ordering.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: Line 420-426 must complete before lines 429-446 execute.

3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: Not applicable to sequencing verification.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: N/A

4_faulty_error_handling.attack_description: Unwrap success but bridge call skipped
4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: After successful unwrap (line 421), code proceeds directly to bridge attempt (line 430). No early return between them.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Successful unwrap -> underlyingTokenAmount set -> bridge called unconditionally.

5_race_conditions.analysis: enableSelfCall modifier only allows self-calls for specific functions. nonReentrant on entry points prevents external reentrancy. Self-call functions have onlySelfCall modifier.
5_race_conditions.counterexample: onlySelfCall functions only callable from within _unwrapAndBridge. No external reentrancy path.

audit_results.summary: Sequential execution enforced via code structure. Bridge only called after successful unwrap completion.

audit_results.title: Verify bridge failure keeps user funds safe

1_input_validation_bypass.attack_description: Funds lost on bridge failure due to missing recovery
1_input_validation_bypass.analysis: Bridge failure caught at line 434. Before bridge, underlyingTokenBalances[user] credited at line 469. On failure, event emitted, balance preserved. User can call withdraw(underlyingToken, amount) at lines 281-284.
1_input_validation_bypass.counterexample: Bridge fails -> underlyingTokenBalances intact -> user calls withdraw() -> funds recovered.

2_state_transition_violation.attack_description: Partial state update on bridge failure
2_state_transition_violation.analysis: _bridgeUnderlyingToken: _debitNativeBalance (line 484) and _debitUnderlyingBalance (line 485) called before Stargate.send. If send fails, balances already debited but transaction reverts entirely.
2_state_transition_violation.counterexample: Stargate.send reverts -> entire _bridgeUnderlyingToken reverts -> debit operations rolled back.

3_resource_exhaustion.analysis: Not applicable.
3_resource_exhaustion.counterexample: N/A

4_faulty_error_handling.attack_description: Bridge failure not caught, funds stuck
4_faulty_error_handling.analysis: bridgeUnderlyingTokenSelf wrapped in try-catch (lines 430-446). All failures caught. Event emitted with error details. User balance preserved for manual withdrawal.
4_faulty_error_handling.counterexample: Any bridge error -> caught -> BridgeUnderlyingTokenFailed event -> user notified -> withdraw funds.
